title: Marketing and market research
description: Compare competitors and substitutes in the named market before proposing positioning or a launch message.
questions: What market, audience and time window should the research cover?
What do dated product pages, release notes, public statements or filings confirm about direct competitors and substitutes?
What can the team substantiate in launch messaging, and which claims need evidence?

sources.title: U.S. Small Business Administration, Market research and competitive analysis
UK Government Communication Service, Campaign lifecycle

specialists.title: Market researcher
specialists.focus: Define the buyer problem, geography and review period. Compare dated evidence for direct competitors, substitutes and the option of doing nothing.

specialists.title: Positioning lead
specialists.focus: Connect audience needs to a specific value proposition. Identify the proof, scope and qualifications needed for claims about capability, outcomes or differentiation.

specialists.title: Channel planner
specialists.focus: Compare how the target audience discovers and evaluates options across channels. Propose a sequence and pilot that fit the budget and production effort.

specialists.title: Marketing measurement analyst
specialists.focus: Define the observable action and attribution limits. Select a baseline or comparison that can distinguish campaign effects from seasonality and other launches.

evidence: Named audience, buying role, market geography, release timing and available campaign capacity.
Approved customer interviews or win-loss notes for the stated problem, with date and segment where available.
Dated product pages, release notes or official statements for relevant competitors. Record the plan, region and version that support each claim.
Approved message claims with their backing release criteria, customer evidence and applicable qualification.
Channel performance baselines, event or reporting definitions and known changes to tracking or visitor mix.
challenge: Test whether the claimed differentiation survives after comparing the same problem, subscription tier, market and time window.
Compare a broader launch, a targeted audience pilot and deferring the launch until an evidence gap closes. State what could change the audience or message.
Challenge claims drawn from a competitor's silence, a small interview sample or traffic without a defined buyer action.
Check if simultaneous launches, seasonality or measurement changes could produce the same outcome without the campaign.
decision_criteria: Recommend a message when the selected audience has a specific evidenced need and every material claim can be supported with appropriately scoped proof.
Recommend a pilot when channel fit, audience behavior or incremental impact is uncertain and one measurable test can resolve it.
Defer a claim when supporting evidence applies to another market, version or audience, or when first-hand evidence remains unavailable.
Recommend a channel only with an owner, a feasible budget and a defined action that the team can measure or validate.
